units.en: But when their flight had taken them past the trench and the set stakes, and many had fallen by the hands of the Danaans, the Trojans made a halt on reaching their chariots, routed and pale with fear. Jove now woke on the crests of Ida, where he was lying with golden-throned Juno by his side, and starting to his feet he saw the Trojans and Achaeans, the one thrown into confusion, and the others driving them pell-mell before them with King Neptune in their midst. He saw Hector lying on the ground with his comrades gathered round him, gasping for breath, wandering in mind and vomiting blood, for it was not the feeblest of the Achaeans who struck him.
units.ja: しかし、逃亡の果てに塹壕と並べられた杭の外まで逃れ出て、多くの者がダナオイ勢の手にかかって倒れると、トロイア勢は戦車のそばまでたどり着いたところで足を止めた。敗走し、恐怖で顔を青ざめさせていた。ゼウスはこのとき、イデ山の峰で目を覚ました。黄金の椅子に座すヘラを傍らに臥していたのだ。彼は立ち上がると、トロイア勢とアカイア勢の姿を見た。一方は混乱に陥り、他方はポセイドン王を真ん中に据えて、相手をめちゃくちゃに追い立てていた。ヘクトルが地面に横たわり、仲間たちがその周りに集まっているのも見えた。息をあえがせ、心はさまよい、血を吐いていた。彼を打ったのは、アカイア勢の中でも最弱の者などではなかったからだ。

notes.title: ダナオイ
notes.body: アカイア勢の別名で、ギリシア側を指す。ホメロスは「アカイア勢」「ダナオイ勢」「アルゲイオイ勢」を言い換えとして用いる。
notes.bodyEn: Another name for the Achaeans, referring to the Greek side. Homer uses "Achaeans," "Danaans," and "Argives" as variants.

units.en: The sire of gods and men had pity on him, and looked fiercely on Juno. “I see, Juno,” said he, “you mischief-making trickster, that your cunning has stayed Hector from fighting and has caused the rout of his host. I am in half a mind to thrash you, in which case you will be the first to reap the fruits of your scurvy knavery. Do you not remember how once upon a time I had you hanged? I fastened two anvils on to your feet, and bound your hands in a chain of gold which none might break, and you hung in mid-air among the clouds. All the gods in Olympus were in a fury, but they could not reach you to set you free; when I caught any one of them I gripped him and hurled him from the heavenly threshold till he came fainting down to earth; yet even this did not relieve my mind from the incessant anxiety which I felt about noble Hercules whom you and Boreas had spitefully conveyed beyond the seas to Cos, after suborning the tempests; but I rescued him, and notwithstanding all his mighty labours I brought him back again to Argos. I would remind you of this that you may learn to leave off being so deceitful, and discover how much you are likely to gain by the embraces out of which you have come here to trick me.”
units.ja: 神々と人々の父はヘクトルを哀れに思い、ヘラを鋭く睨みつけた。「ヘラよ」と彼は言った。「お前の悪だくみがヘクトルを戦いから遠ざけ、彼の軍勢を敗走させたのだな、この厄介者の謀りごと師め。今にもお前を打ち据えてやりたい気分だ。そうなれば、お前は自分の卑劣な悪巧みの最初の報いを受けることになる。覚えているか、むかし一度お前を宙吊りにしたことを。お前の両足には金床を二つ結びつけ、両手は誰も断ち切れぬ金の鎖で縛り、お前は雲の間の宙にぶら下がっていた。オリュンポスの神々は皆激怒したが、お前のところへ届いて自由にしてやることはできなかった。私が誰かを見つけて捕まえると、その者を天の敷居から投げ落とし、気を失って地上に落ちるまでにした。それでも私の心は、絶えず抱えていた悩みから解放されなかった。高貴なヘラクレスのことだ。お前とボレアスは、嵐を唆して彼を海の向こうのコス島へ意地悪く運び去った。しかし私は彼を救い出し、あまたの難業にもかかわらず彼を再びアルゴスへ連れ戻した。このことを言っておくのは、お前がそうした欺瞞をやめることを学び、私を欺こうと抱擁のうちからここへやって来たその抱擁によって、どれほどのものを得る見込みかを思い知るためだ。」

units.en: Juno trembled as he spoke, and said, “May heaven above and earth below be my witnesses, with the waters of the river Styx—and this is the most solemn oath that a blessed god can take—nay, I swear also by your own almighty head and by our bridal bed—things over which I could never possibly perjure myself—that Neptune is not punishing Hector and the Trojans and helping the Achaeans through any doing of mine; it is all of his own mere motion because he was sorry to see the Achaeans hard pressed at their ships: if I were advising him, I should tell him to do as you bid him.”
units.ja: ヘラは彼が語るうちに震え、こう言った。「天の上も地の下も、そしてスティクス川の水も、私の証人となってください。これは幸いなる神が立てうる最も厳粛な誓いです。いえ、あなたご自身の全能の頭にかけて、そして私たちの婚姻の床にかけても誓います。それらについて、私が偽りの誓いを立てることなど決してありえません。ポセイドンがヘクトルとトロイア勢を罰し、アカイア勢を助けているのは、少しも私の仕業ではありません。すべて彼自身の勝手な思いからで、アカイア勢が船のそばで追い詰められるのを見て哀れに思ったからです。もし私が彼に助言するなら、あなたが命じたようにするよう申しましょう。」

notes.title: スティクス川
notes.body: 冥界を流れる川で、神々が誓いを立てる際に呼び出す証人。偽りの誓いには厳しい罰が下るとされる。
notes.bodyEn: The river that flows through the underworld, the witness the gods invoke when they swear an oath. A false oath is said to bring down severe punishment.

units.en: The sire of gods and men smiled and answered, “If you, Juno, were always to support me when we sit in council of the gods, Neptune, like it or no, would soon come round to your and my way of thinking. If, then, you are speaking the truth and mean what you say, go among the rank and file of the gods, and tell Iris and Apollo lord of the bow, that I want them—Iris, that she may go to the Achaean host and tell Neptune to leave off fighting and go home, and Apollo, that he may send Hector again into battle and give him fresh strength; he will thus forget his present sufferings, and drive the Achaeans back in confusion till they fall among the ships of Achilles son of Peleus. Achilles will then send his comrade Patroclus into battle, and Hector will kill him in front of Ilius after he has slain many warriors, and among them my own noble son Sarpedon. Achilles will kill Hector to avenge Patroclus, and from that time I will bring it about that the Achaeans shall persistently drive the Trojans back till they fulfil the counsels of Minerva and take Ilius. But I will not stay my anger, nor permit any god to help the Danaans till I have accomplished the desire of the son of Peleus, according to the promise I made by bowing my head on the day when Thetis touched my knees and besought me to give him honour.”
units.ja: 神々と人々の父は微笑んで答えた。「ヘラよ、お前がいつも神々の議会で私を支持してくれるなら、ポセイドンも、好むと好まざるとにかかわらず、まもなくお前と私の考えに従うだろう。それなら、お前が真実を語り、言うことに偽りがないのなら、神々の列の間へ行き、イリスと弓の主アポロンに、私が二人を呼んでいると伝えよ。イリスには、アカイア勢の陣へ行ってポセイドンに戦いをやめて家へ帰れと告げるために。アポロンには、ヘクトルを再び戦場へ送り返して新たな力を与えるために。そうすれば彼は今の苦しみを忘れ、アカイア勢を混乱のうちに追い返し、ペレウスの子アキレウスの船のところまで追い詰めるだろう。そのときアキレウスは戦友パトロクロスを戦いへ送り出し、ヘクトルはイリオスの前でパトロクロスを殺す。その前にヘクトルは多くの戦士を殺し、その中には私の高貴な息子サルペドンもいる。アキレウスはパトロクロスの仇を討つためヘクトルを殺し、その時から私は、アカイア勢がアテナの計略を成就させ、イリオスを陥落させるまで、トロイア勢を執拗に追い返すよう取り計らう。しかし、私がペレウスの子の望みを果たし、テティスが私の膝にすがって彼に名誉を与えるよう願った日に、頭をうなずけて立てた約束を果たすまでは、私の怒りを収めもせず、ダナオイ勢を助けることをどの神にも許しもしない。」

notes.title: 頭をうなずけての約束
notes.body: ゼウスが頭をうなずいて示した約束は、取り消しのきかない絶対の確約とされる。テティスはアキレウスの母で、ゼウスに息子の名誉回復を願った。
notes.titleEn: The promise made with a nod of the head
notes.bodyEn: The promise Zeus indicated with a nod of his head is held to be an absolute pledge that cannot be revoked. Thetis is Achilles' mother, and she asked Zeus to restore her son's honor.

units.en: Juno heeded his words and went from the heights of Ida to great Olympus. Swift as the thought of one whose fancy carries him over vast continents, and he says to himself, “Now I will be here, or there,” and he would have all manner of things—even so swiftly did Juno wing her way till she came to high Olympus and went in among the gods who were gathered in the house of Jove. When they saw her they all of them came up to her, and held out their cups to her by way of greeting. She let the others be, but took the cup offered her by lovely Themis, who was first to come running up to her. “Juno,” said she, “why are you here? And you seem troubled—has your husband the son of Saturn been frightening you?”
units.ja: ヘラはその言葉に従い、イデ山の峰から大いなるオリュンポスへと赴いた。広い大陸を越えて空想に運ばれる者の思いのように、その者は「今はここに、いやあそこに」と心に言い、あらゆるものを望む。まさにその速さでヘラは羽ばたき、高いオリュンポスに着き、ゼウスの館に集まった神々の間へ入っていった。神々は彼女を見ると皆そばへ寄り、挨拶として酒杯を差し出した。彼女は他の者たちには構わず、最初に走り寄ってきた美しいテミスが差し出す杯を受け取った。「ヘラよ」とテミスは言った。「どうしてここへ。そして思い悩んでいるようだが、夫のクロノスの子があなたを怖がらせたのか。」

units.en: And Juno answered, “Themis, do not ask me about it. You know what a proud and cruel disposition my husband has. Lead the gods to table, where you and all the immortals can hear the wicked designs which he has avowed. Many a one, mortal and immortal, will be angered by them, however peaceably he may be feasting now.”
units.ja: ヘラは答えた。「テミスよ、そのことを私に尋ねないでください。あなたは私の夫がどれほど高慢で残酷な気性かを知っているでしょう。神々を食卓へ導いてください。そこであなたもすべての不死の者たちも、彼が公言した邪悪な企てを聞くことができます。今どれほど穏やかに宴を楽しんでいても、その企てに怒りを覚える者は、人間でも神でも多いことでしょう。」

units.en: On this Juno sat down, and the gods were troubled throughout the house of Jove. Laughter sat on her lips but her brow was furrowed with care, and she spoke up in a rage. “Fools that we are,” she cried, “to be thus madly angry with Jove; we keep on wanting to go up to him and stay him by force or by persuasion, but he sits aloof and cares for nobody, for he knows that he is much stronger than any other of the immortals. Make the best, therefore, of whatever ills he may choose to send each one of you; Mars, I take it, has had a taste of them already, for his son Ascalaphus has fallen in battle—the man whom of all others he loved most dearly and whose father he owns himself to be.”
units.ja: そこでヘラは腰を下ろし、ゼウスの館の神々は騒然となった。彼女の唇には笑みがあったが、その額には心配の皺が刻まれ、彼女は怒りを込めて口を開いた。「なんと愚かなことでしょう、私たちは」と彼女は叫んだ。「こうしてゼウスに対して狂ったように怒っているのです。私たちは彼のところへ行き、力ずくか説得で彼を引き止めようとし続けていますが、彼は遠く離れて座り、誰も気に留めません。他のどの不死の者よりも自分がはるかに強いと知っているからです。ですから、彼があなた方一人一人に送ろうとするいかなる災いも、できるだけうまく受け止めなさい。アレスはすでにその味を知っているはずです。彼の息子アスカラポスが戦いで倒れたのですから。彼が誰よりも深く愛し、自分の子であると認める者でした。」

notes.title: アレス
notes.body: 戦いを司る神。原文の Mars はローマ名で、ギリシア名はアレス。
notes.bodyEn: The god who governs battle. "Mars" in the source text is the Roman name; the Greek name is Ares.

units.en: When he heard this Mars smote his two sturdy thighs with the flat of his hands, and said in anger, “Do not blame me, you gods that dwell in heaven, if I go to the ships of the Achaeans and avenge the death of my son, even though it end in my being struck by Jove’s lightning and lying in blood and dust among the corpses.”
units.ja: これを聞いてアレスは、両のたくましい腿を手のひらで打ち、怒りを込めて言った。「天に住む神々よ、私がアカイア勢の船へ行き、息子の死の仇を討っても、私を責めないでください。たとえそれが、ゼウスの雷に打たれ、死体の間に血と塵にまみれて横たわる結末になろうとも。」

units.en: As he spoke he gave orders to yoke his horses Panic and Rout, while he put on his armour. On this, Jove would have been roused to still more fierce and implacable enmity against the other immortals, had not Minerva, alarmed for the safety of the gods, sprung from her seat and hurried outside. She tore the helmet from his head and the shield from his shoulders, and she took the bronze spear from his strong hand and set it on one side; then she said to Mars, “Madman, you are undone; you have ears that hear not, or you have lost all judgement and understanding; have you not heard what Juno has said on coming straight from the presence of Olympian Jove? Do you wish to go through all kinds of suffering before you are brought back sick and sorry to Olympus, after having caused infinite mischief to all us others? Jove would instantly leave the Trojans and Achaeans to themselves; he would come to Olympus to punish us, and would grip us up one after another, guilty or not guilty. Therefore lay aside your anger for the death of your son; better men than he have either been killed already or will fall hereafter, and one cannot protect every one’s whole family.”
units.ja: そう言いながら彼は、自分の馬である「恐慌」と「潰走」に軛をつけるよう命じ、武具を身につけた。このとき、神々の安全を案じたアテナが席を蹴って外へ急ぎ出なければ、ゼウスは他の不死の者たちに対してさらに激しく和解しがたい敵意を抱いたことだろう。彼女は彼の頭から兜を、肩から盾をもぎ取り、その強い手から青銅の槍を取って脇へ置いた。そしてアレスに言った。「狂人よ、あなたはもうおしまいだ。聞こえない耳を持っているか、あるいは判断力も理解も失っているかのどちらかだ。ヘラが、オリュンポスのゼウスの面前からまっすぐに来て言ったことを聞かなかったのか。私たち皆に限りない災いを引き起こしたあげく、病み、後悔しつつオリュンポスへ連れ戻される前に、あらゆる苦しみを味わいたいのか。ゼウスはただちにトロイア勢とアカイア勢を放っておき、オリュンポスへ来て私たちを罰し、有罪か無罪かに関わらず一人ずつ捕まえて吊るすだろう。だから息子の死への怒りは捨てなさい。彼よりも優れた者たちも、すでに殺されたか、これから倒れるのだ。誰も皆の家族を守ることなどできない。」

notes.title: 「恐慌」と「潰走」
notes.body: アレスが駆る二頭の馬で、原文の名は「恐怖」「敗走」を意味する。戦場に伴う心理そのものを擬人化した名とされる。
notes.bodyEn: The two horses Ares drives; their names in the source text mean "fear" and "rout." They are held to be names that personify the very psychology that accompanies the battlefield.

units.en: With these words she took Mars back to his seat. Meanwhile Juno called Apollo outside, with Iris the messenger of the gods. “Jove,” she said to them, “desires you to go to him at once on Mt. Ida; when you have seen him you are to do as he may then bid you.”
units.ja: こう言って彼女はアレスを席へ連れ戻した。その間にヘラは、神々の使者イリスとともにアポロンを外へ呼び出した。「ゼウスが」と彼女は二人に言った。「すぐにイデ山の彼のもとへ行くことを望んでいます。彼に会ったら、そのとき彼が命じるままにしなさい。」

units.en: Thereon Juno left them and resumed her seat inside, while Iris and Apollo made all haste on their way. When they reached many-fountained Ida, mother of wild beasts, they found Jove seated on topmost Gargarus with a fragrant cloud encircling his head as with a diadem. They stood before his presence, and he was pleased with them for having been so quick in obeying the orders his wife had given them.
units.ja: そこでヘラは二人を残して中へ戻り、自分の席に着いた。イリスとアポロンは急いで道を進んだ。野獣の母である泉の多いイデ山に着くと、彼らはゼウスがガルガロスの頂に座し、香しい雲が冠のようにその頭を囲んでいるのを見つけた。彼らはその前に立ち、妻が与えた命令にすぐ従ったことを彼は喜んだ。

notes.title: ガルガロス
notes.body: イデ山の最高峰。ゼウスが戦場を見渡す座として描かれる。
notes.bodyEn: The highest peak of Mount Ida. It is depicted as the seat from which Zeus surveys the battlefield.

units.en: He spoke to Iris first. “Go,” said he, “fleet Iris, tell King Neptune what I now bid you—and tell him true. Bid him leave off fighting, and either join the company of the gods, or go down into the sea. If he takes no heed and disobeys me, let him consider well whether he is strong enough to hold his own against me if I attack him. I am older and much stronger than he is; yet he is not afraid to set himself up as on a level with myself, of whom all the other gods stand in awe.”
units.ja: 彼はまずイリスに語りかけた。『行け』と彼は言った。『疾風のイリスよ、今わしが命じることを王ポセイドンに伝えよ——そして偽りなく伝えよ。戦いをやめ、神々の仲間に加わるか、海へ下るかせよ、と彼に命じよ。もし彼が聞き入れず、わしに背くなら、わしが攻めかかったとき、彼はわしに立ち向かえるほど強いのかどうか、よく考えるがよい。わしは彼より年長で、はるかに強いのだ。それなのに彼は、他の神々がみな畏れ敬うわしと自分を同格に置くことを、恐れもせずにしている。』

notes.title: イリス
notes.body: 虹の女神で、神々、とりわけゼウスの伝令を務める。ここではゼウスの使いとしてポセイドンのもとへ遣わされる。
notes.bodyEn: The goddess of the rainbow, who serves as messenger to the gods, and above all to Zeus. Here she is sent as Zeus's envoy to Poseidon.

units.en: Iris, fleet as the wind, obeyed him, and as the cold hail or snow-flakes that fly from out the clouds before the blast of Boreas, even so did she wing her way till she came close up to the great shaker of the earth. Then she said, “I have come, O dark-haired king that holds the world in his embrace, to bring you a message from Jove. He bids you leave off fighting, and either join the company of the gods or go down into the sea; if, however, you take no heed and disobey him, he says he will come down here and fight you. He would have you keep out of his reach, for he is older and much stronger than you are, and yet you are not afraid to set yourself up as on a level with himself, of whom all the other gods stand in awe.”
units.ja: 疾風のように速いイリスはそれに従った。そして、ボレアスの吹きすさぶ風の前に雲から飛び来る冷たい雹や雪片のように、大いなる大地を揺るがす者のすぐそばへ飛んでいった。そこで彼女は言った。『世界をその抱擁に抱く黒髪の王よ、わたくしはゼウスからの伝言を携えて参りました。彼はあなたに、戦いをやめ、神々の仲間に加わるか、海へ下るかせよ、と命じておられます。しかしもしあなたが聞き入れず、彼に背かれるなら、彼はここへ降りてあなたと戦うであろう、とも申しておられます。彼はあなたを自分の手の届かぬところに置いておきたいのです。彼はあなたより年長で、はるかに強いのですから。それなのにあなたは、他の神々がみな畏れ敬う彼と自分を同格に置くことを、恐れもせずにしておられます。』

units.en: Neptune was very angry and said, “Great heavens! strong as Jove may be, he has said more than he can do if he has threatened violence against me, who am of like honour with himself. We were three brothers whom Rhea bore to Saturn—Jove, myself, and Hades who rules the world below. Heaven and earth were divided into three parts, and each of us was to have an equal share. When we cast lots, it fell to me to have my dwelling in the sea for evermore; Hades took the darkness of the realms under the earth, while air and sky and clouds were the portion that fell to Jove; but earth and great Olympus are the common property of all. Therefore I will not walk as Jove would have me. For all his strength, let him keep to his own third share and be contented without threatening to lay hands upon me as though I were nobody. Let him keep his bragging talk for his own sons and daughters, who must perforce obey him.”
units.ja: ポセイドンはひどく怒って言った。『おお、天よ。ゼウスはどれほど強いにせよ、このわしに暴力を振るうと脅すとは、できる以上のことを言ったものだ。わしは彼と同じ名誉を持つ者なのだから。わしらはレアがクロノスとの間にもうけた三人の兄弟——ゼウス、わし、そして地下の世界を治めるハデス——であった。天と地は三つに分けられ、わしらのそれぞれが等しい取り分を持つことになっていた。くじを引くと、わしには永遠に海を住まいとすることが当たった。ハデスは地下の国の暗闇を取った。そして空気と天と雲がゼウスの取り分となった。しかし大地と大いなるオリュンポスは、すべての者の共有のものである。それゆえわしは、ゼウスが望むままには歩みはしない。彼の力が何であろうと、自分の三分の一の取り分を守り、わしを何者でもないかのように手にかけようと脅さずに満足していればよい。あの大言壮語は、自分の息子や娘たちに取っておくがよい。彼らは否応なく彼に従わねばならないのだから。』

notes.title: 世界の三分割
notes.body: ゼウス・ポセイドン・ハデスの三兄弟がくじで領分を分けたという説話。ここでは天・海・冥界を三人で分け合い、大地とオリュンポスは共有とされる。
notes.titleEn: The threefold division of the world
notes.bodyEn: The tale that the three brothers Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades divided their domains by lot. Here the three share out heaven, sea, and underworld, while the earth and Olympus are held in common.

units.en: Iris fleet as the wind then answered, “Am I really, Neptune, to take this daring and unyielding message to Jove, or will you reconsider your answer? Sensible people are open to argument, and you know that the Erinyes always range themselves on the side of the older person.”
units.ja: 疾風のように速いイリスはそこで答えた。『ポセイドンよ、わたくしは本当に、この大胆で断固とした伝言をゼウスへ持って行くべきでしょうか。それとも、あなたはお答えをお考え直しになりますか。分別ある者は論に耳を貸すものです。そしてあなたもご存じのとおり、エリニュエスは常に年長の者の側に立つのです。』

notes.title: エリニュエス
notes.body: 復讐と呪いを司る女神たち。ここでは、年長者の側に立つ存在として引き合いに出されている。
notes.bodyEn: The goddesses who govern vengeance and curses. Here they are invoked as beings who stand on the side of the elder.

units.en: Neptune answered, “Goddess Iris, your words have been spoken in season. It is well when a messenger shows so much discretion. Nevertheless it cuts me to the very heart that any one should rebuke so angrily another who is his own peer, and of like empire with himself. Now, however, I will give way in spite of my displeasure; furthermore let me tell you, and I mean what I say—if contrary to the desire of myself, Minerva driver of the spoil, Juno, Mercury, and King Vulcan, Jove spares steep Ilius, and will not let the Achaeans have the great triumph of sacking it, let him understand that he will incur our implacable resentment.”
units.ja: ポセイドンは答えた。『女神イリスよ、あなたの言葉は折を得て語られた。使者がこれほど分別を示すのはよいことだ。とはいえ、自分と同格で同じ支配権を持つ者を、これほど怒りにまかせて責める者がいるとは、わしの心を深くえぐる。しかし今は、不快ではあるが譲ろう。さらに、わしが言うことの意味をよく心得ておくように——わし自身、戦利品を駆るアテナ、ヘラ、ヘルメス、そして王ヘパイストスの望みに反して、ゼウスが切り立ったイリオスを助け、アカイア勢にこれを攻め落とすという大いなる栄誉を与えぬなら、彼はわしらの容赦ない怒りを買うことを、よく承知するがよい。』

notes.title: イリオス
notes.body: トロイア市の別名。ここでは「切り立った」都城として言及され、その救援が神々の対立の争点となっている。
notes.bodyEn: Another name for the city of Troy. Here it is mentioned as a "steep" citadel, and its rescue is the point at issue in the conflict among the gods.

units.en: Neptune now left the field to go down under the sea, and sorely did the Achaeans miss him. Then Jove said to Apollo, “Go, dear Phoebus, to Hector, for Neptune who holds the earth in his embrace has now gone down under the sea to avoid the severity of my displeasure. Had he not done so those gods who are below with Saturn would have come to hear of the fight between us. It is better for both of us that he should have curbed his anger and kept out of my reach, for I should have had much trouble with him. Take, then, your tasselled aegis, and shake it furiously, so as to set the Achaean heroes in a panic; take, moreover, brave Hector, O Far-Darter, into your own care, and rouse him to deeds of daring, till the Achaeans are sent flying back to their ships and to the Hellespont. From that point I will think it well over, how the Achaeans may have a respite from their troubles.”
units.ja: ポセイドンはこうして戦場を去って海の下へ下り、アカイア勢は彼をひどく恋しがった。そこでゼウスはアポロンに言った。『行け、親しきポイボスよ、ヘクトルのもとへ。大地をその抱擁に収めるポセイドンは、わしの怒りの厳しさを避けて、今や海の下へ下った。もしそうしなかったなら、クロノスとともに地下にいる神々が、わしらの間の争いを耳にしたであろう。彼が怒りを抑えてわしの手の届かぬところに身を置いたのは、わしら双方にとってよかったのだ。さもなければ、わしは彼にひどく手を焼くことになっただろう。それゆえ、房飾りのついたアイギスを取り、それを激しく振って、アカイアの勇士たちを恐慌に陥れよ。さらに、勇ましいヘクトルを、遠矢を射る者よ、あなた自身の守りに受け取り、アカイア勢が船とヘレスポントスへ追い返されるまで、彼を大胆な行いへと駆り立てよ。その時から、アカイア勢が苦難からひとときの息をつくにはどうしたらよいか、わしがよく考えよう。』

notes.title: アイギス
notes.body: ゼウス（またアテナ）が持つとされる防具。ここでは、激しく振ると敵に恐慌を起こす力を持つものとして扱われている。
notes.bodyEn: The armor said to be held by Zeus (and also by Athena). Here it is treated as having the power, when shaken violently, to throw the enemy into panic.

units.en: Apollo obeyed his father’s saying, and left the crests of Ida, flying like a falcon, bane of doves and swiftest of all birds. He found Hector no longer lying upon the ground, but sitting up, for he had just come to himself again. He knew those who were about him, and the sweat and hard breathing had left him from the moment when the will of aegis-bearing Jove had revived him. Apollo stood beside him and said, “Hector son of Priam, why are you so faint, and why are you here away from the others? Has any mishap befallen you?”
units.ja: アポロンは父の言葉に従い、鳩を殺す鳥、すべての鳥のうちで最も速い隼のように飛んで、イデの峰々を去った。彼が見出したヘクトルは、もはや地面に横たわってはおらず、身を起こして座っていた。ちょうど我に返ったところだったのだ。彼は自分の周りにいる者たちを見分けており、汗と荒い息は、アイギスを持つゼウスの意志が彼を蘇らせたその瞬間から去っていた。アポロンは彼のそばに立ち、言った。『プリアモスの子ヘクトルよ、なぜお前はそんなに弱っているのか、なぜ他の者たちから離れてここにいるのか。何か災難がお前に降りかかったのか。』

units.en: Hector in a weak voice answered, “And which, kind sir, of the gods are you, who now ask me thus? Do you not know that Ajax struck me on the chest with a stone as I was killing his comrades at the ships of the Achaeans, and compelled me to leave off fighting? I made sure that this very day I should breathe my last and go down into the house of Hades.”
units.ja: ヘクトルは弱々しい声で答えた。『親切な方よ、こうしてわしに問うあなたは、神々のうちのどなたですか。あなたはご存じないのですか。わしがアカイア勢の船のそばで彼の仲間たちを殺しているとき、アイアスが石をわしの胸に投げつけ、戦いをやめざるを得なくさせたのです。わしは、まさにこの日に息を引き取り、ハデスの館へ下るのだと確信しておりました。』

units.en: Then King Apollo said to him, “Take heart; the son of Saturn has sent you a mighty helper from Ida to stand by you and defend you, even me, Phoebus Apollo of the golden sword, who have been guardian hitherto not only of yourself but of your city. Now, therefore, order your horsemen to drive their chariots to the ships in great multitudes. I will go before your horses to smooth the way for them, and will turn the Achaeans in flight.”
units.ja: そこで王アポロンは彼に言った。『元気を出せ。クロノスの子は、お前を支え守る強力な助っ人をイデから遣わしたのだ。このわし、黄金の剣を持つポイボス・アポロン、これまでお前だけでなくお前の都の守護者でもあった者を。だから今、お前の騎兵たちに命じて、多数の戦車を船めがけて駆らせよ。わしがお前の馬の前に立って道をならし、アカイア勢を敗走させよう。』

units.en: As he spoke he infused great strength into the shepherd of his people. And as a horse, stabled and full-fed, breaks loose and gallops gloriously over the plain to the place where he is wont to take his bath in the river—he tosses his head, and his mane streams over his shoulders as in all the pride of his strength he flies full speed to the pastures where the mares are feeding—even so Hector, when he heard what the god said, urged his horsemen on, and sped forward as fast as his limbs could take him. As country peasants set their hounds on to a homed stag or wild goat—he has taken shelter under rock or thicket, and they cannot find him, but, lo, a bearded lion whom their shouts have roused stands in their path, and they are in no further humour for the chase—even so the Achaeans were still charging on in a body, using their swords and spears pointed at both ends, but when they saw Hector going about among his men they were afraid, and their hearts fell down into their feet.
units.ja: こう語りながら、彼は民の牧者に大いなる力を吹き込んだ。厩につながれ、十分に飼い葉を与えられた馬が解き放たれ、川で水浴びをするいつもの場所へ向かって、平原を意気揚々と駆けていくように——頭を振り、たてがみを肩に流し、力の誇りに満ちて、牝馬たちが草を食む牧場へ全速力で飛んでいく——まさにそのように、ヘクトルは神の言葉を聞くと、騎兵たちをせき立て、四肢の許す限り速く前へ飛び出した。いなかの農夫たちが、角のある牡鹿や野山羊に猟犬をけしかけるように——獲物は岩や藪の下に身を隠し、彼らはそれを見つけられない。ところが、見よ、彼らの叫び声に呼び覚まされた鬚のある獅子が道に立ちふさがり、彼らはもう追跡どころではなくなる——まさにそのように、アカイア勢はまだ一団となって突撃し、剣と、両端に穂先のある槍を使っていたが、ヘクトルが自分の部下たちの間を行き来しているのを見ると、恐れをなし、心が足元へ落ちる思いだった。

notes.title: ホメロス的直喩
notes.body: 馬や狩りの情景を長く描いてから「まさにそのように」と戦場へ戻る、叙事詩特有の引き延ばされた直喩。ここではヘクトルの勢いと、アカイア勢の恐れが対照的に描かれる。
notes.bodyEn: The extended simile peculiar to epic: a scene of horses or of hunting is described at length, and then the poem returns to the battlefield with "even so." Here the momentum of Hector and the fear of the Achaeans are set out in contrast.

units.en: Then spoke Thoas son of Andraemon, leader of the Aetolians, a man who could throw a good throw, and who was staunch also in close fight, while few could surpass him in debate when opinions were divided. He then with all sincerity and goodwill addressed them thus: “What, in heaven’s name, do I now see? Is it not Hector come to life again? Every one made sure he had been killed by Ajax son of Telamon, but it seems that one of the gods has again rescued him. He has killed many of us Danaans already, and I take it will yet do so, for the hand of Jove must be with him or he would never dare show himself so masterful in the forefront of the battle. Now, therefore, let us all do as I say; let us order the main body of our forces to fall back upon the ships, but let those of us who profess to be the flower of the army stand firm, and see whether we cannot hold Hector back at the point of our spears as soon as he comes near us; I conceive that he will then think better of it before he tries to charge into the press of the Danaans.”
units.ja: そこでアンドライモンの子トアスが語った。アイトリア人の指導者であり、槍投げの巧い男、接近戦でも屈強な男で、意見が分かれたときの議論では彼に勝てる者はほとんどいなかった。彼は真心と好意をもって、彼らにこう語りかけた。『おお、いったい何事だ、今わしは何を見ているのか。死んだはずのヘクトルが生き返ったのではないか。誰もが彼はテラモンの子アイアスに討たれたと確信していたが、どうやら神々のうちの一人が彼をまた救い出したらしい。彼はすでに多くのダナオス勢を殺し、これからも殺すだろう。ゼウスの手が彼とともにあるのでなければ、彼があれほど戦いの最前列で威張り散らすなど、決してできはしない。だから今、皆わしの言うとおりにせよ。わしらの軍の本体には船へ退くよう命じ、しかし軍の精鋭と自称する者たちは踏みとどまり、彼が近づき次第、槍の穂先で彼を食い止められるかどうか見てみよう。わしの考えでは、彼はダナオス勢の群れへ突撃しようとする前に、よく考え直すだろう。』

notes.title: ダナオス勢
notes.body: アカイア勢と同じ集団を指す呼び名。ギリシア側はアカイア勢、ダナオス勢、アルゴス勢など複数の呼称で呼ばれ、韻律に応じて使い分けられる。
notes.bodyEn: A name for the same group as the Achaeans. The Greek side is called by several names—Achaeans, Danaans, Argives, and others—which are used as the meter requires.

units.en: Thus did he speak, and they did even as he had said. Those who were about Ajax and King Idomeneus, the followers moreover of Teucer, Meriones, and Meges peer of Mars called all their best men about them and sustained the fight against Hector and the Trojans, but the main body fell back upon the ships of the Achaeans.
units.ja: 彼はこう語り、彼らは彼の言ったとおりにした。アイアスと王イドメネウスの周りの者たち、さらにテウクロス、メリオネス、そして軍神アレスに匹敵するメゲスの従者たちは、最良の者たちを自分の周りに呼び集め、ヘクトルとトロイア勢に対する戦いを支え続けた。しかし本体はアカイア勢の船へと退いた。

units.en: The Trojans pressed forward in a dense body, with Hector striding on at their head. Before him went Phoebus Apollo shrouded in cloud about his shoulders. He bore aloft the terrible aegis with its shaggy fringe, which Vulcan the smith had given Jove to strike terror into the hearts of men. With this in his hand he led on the Trojans.
units.ja: トロイア勢は密集した隊列で押し進み、その先頭ではヘクトルが大股に歩いていた。彼の前には、両肩のまわりを雲に包まれたポイボス・アポロンが進んだ。アポロンは、毛の房のついた恐ろしいアイギスを高く掲げていた。それは、人間の心に恐怖を刻むために、鍛冶の神ヘパイストスがゼウスに与えたものだった。アポロンはこれを手にして、トロイア勢を導いた。

notes.title: アイギス
notes.body: 「アイギス」はゼウスの恐ろしい護りで、振りかざされると人間に恐怖を与えるとされる。本段落ではアポロンがこれを掲げて、トロイア勢を導く。
notes.bodyEn: The "aegis" is Zeus's fearsome protection, and when brandished it is said to strike terror into humans. In this paragraph Apollo raises it and leads the Trojans.

units.en: The Argives held together and stood their ground. The cry of battle rose high from either side, and the arrows flew from the bowstrings. Many a spear sped from strong hands and fastened in the bodies of many a valiant warrior, while others fell to earth midway, before they could taste of man’s fair flesh and glut themselves with blood. So long as Phoebus Apollo held his aegis quietly and without shaking it, the weapons on either side took effect and the people fell, but when he shook it straight in the face of the Danaans and raised his mighty battle-cry their hearts fainted within them and they forgot their former prowess. As when two wild beasts spring in the dead of night on a herd of cattle or a large flock of sheep when the herdsman is not there—even so were the Danaans struck helpless, for Apollo filled them with panic and gave victory to Hector and the Trojans.
units.ja: アルゴス勢は隊を固めて持ちこたえた。両軍から鬨の声が高く上がり、矢が弦から飛び出した。多くの槍が力強い手から放たれ、多くの勇敢な戦士の体に突き立った。一方、他の槍は途中で大地に落ち、人間の美しい肉を味わうことも、血に飽きることもなかった。ポイボス・アポロンがアイギスを静かに、揺さぶらずに保っているかぎりは、双方の武器は効をなし、兵たちは倒れていった。しかしアポロンがダナオイ勢の面前でそれを振りかざし、力強い鬨の声を上げると、彼らの胸中の心は萎え、それまでの武勇を忘れてしまった。夜も更けたころ、牛の群れや、羊飼いのいない大きな羊の群れに二頭の野獣が飛びかかるように——ダナオイ勢はなすすべもなく打ちのめされた。アポロンが彼らを恐慌で満たし、ヘクトルとトロイア勢に勝利を与えたからである。

notes.title: ギリシア勢の呼び名
notes.body: 「アルゴス勢」「ダナオイ勢」はどちらもギリシア側の軍を指す呼称で、「アカイア勢」と同じ相手を指す。原語では一つの集団を複数の名で呼び分けている。
notes.bodyEn: "Argives" and "Danaans" are both names for the Greek army and refer to the same side as "Achaeans." In the original language a single group is called by several different names.

units.en: The fight then became more scattered and they killed one another where they best could. Hector killed Stichius and Arcesilaus, the one, leader of the Boeotians, and the other, friend and comrade of Menestheus. Aeneas killed Medon and Iasus. The first was bastard son to Oileus, and brother to Ajax, but he lived in Phylace away from his own country, for he had killed a man, a kinsman of his stepmother Eriopis whom Oileus had married. Iasus had become a leader of the Athenians, and was son of Sphelus the son of Boucolos. Polydamas killed Mecisteus, and Polites Echius, in the front of the battle, while Agenor slew Clonius. Paris struck Deiochus from behind in the lower part of the shoulder, as he was flying among the foremost, and the point of the spear went clean through him.
units.ja: 戦いはそのとき、より散開したものとなり、両軍はそれぞれ手の届くところで殺し合った。ヘクトルはスティキオスとアルケシラオスを討った。一人はボイオティア勢の指揮官であり、もう一人はメネステウスの友であり僚友であった。アイネイアスはメドンとイアソスを討った。前者はオイレウスの庶子で、アイアスの兄弟であったが、自分の国を離れてピュラケに住んでいた。義母エリオピス——オイレウスが妻に迎えた女——の血族を一人殺したからである。イアソスはアテナイ勢の指揮官となっており、ブコロスの子スペルスの子であった。ポリュダマスはメキステウスを、ポリテスは最前線でエキオスを討ち、アゲノルはクロニオスを殺した。パリスは、デイオコスが最前列のあいだを逃げ回っているところを、背後から肩の下部に突き刺した。槍の穂先は彼をまっすぐに貫いた。

notes.title: アイアス（オイレウスの子）
notes.body: ここでメドンの兄弟とされるアイアスは、オイレウスの子アイアス（小アイアス）。同じ名を持つ大アイアス（テラモンの子）とは別人物である。
notes.bodyEn: The Ajax said here to be Medon's brother is Ajax, son of Oileus (Little Ajax). He is a different man from the Ajax of the same name, Great Ajax (son of Telamon).

units.en: While they were spoiling these heroes of their armour, the Achaeans were flying pell-mell to the trench and the set stakes, and were forced back within their wall. Hector then cried out to the Trojans, “Forward to the ships, and let the spoils be. If I see any man keeping back on the other side the wall away from the ships I will have him killed: his kinsmen and kinswomen shall not give him his dues of fire, but dogs shall tear him in pieces in front of our city.”
units.ja: 彼らがこれらの勇士たちの武具を剥ぎ取っているあいだに、アカイア勢は壕と立てられた杭の方へ我先にと逃げ、自分たちの城壁の内側へと押し戻されていた。そこでヘクトルはトロイア勢に叫んだ。「船へ進め、戦利品は捨て置け。城壁の向こう側で、船から離れて後ろに残っている男を見つけたなら、その男は殺す。その者の親族の男も女も、火を焚く礼を彼に与えることはできない。犬どもがわれらの町の前で彼をずたずたに引き裂くであろう。」

notes.title: 火葬を奪うという脅し
notes.body: 死者を火で葬ることは古代ギリシアで最も重い務めとされ、それを与えないという脅しは、遺体を辱め、埋葬そのものを奪うことを意味する。
notes.bodyEn: Burying the dead with fire was held in ancient Greece to be the weightiest of duties, and the threat to deny it means to dishonor the corpse and to deprive it of burial itself.

units.en: As he spoke he laid his whip about his horses’ shoulders and called to the Trojans throughout their ranks; the Trojans shouted with a cry that rent the air, and kept their horses neck and neck with his own. Phoebus Apollo went before, and kicked down the banks of the deep trench into its middle so as to make a great broad bridge, as broad as the throw of a spear when a man is trying his strength. The Trojan battalions poured over the bridge, and Apollo with his redoubtable aegis led the way. He kicked down the wall of the Achaeans as easily as a child who playing on the sea-shore has built a house of sand and then kicks it down again and destroys it—even so did you, O Apollo, shed toil and trouble upon the Argives, filling them with panic and confusion.
units.ja: こう言ってヘクトルは、馬たちの肩に鞭を打ちつけ、隊列のいたるところでトロイア勢に呼びかけた。トロイア勢は空気を裂くような叫びを上げ、馬を彼の馬と首を並べて進めた。ポイボス・アポロンが先に立ち、深い壕の土手を蹴り崩して壕の真ん中へ落とし、槍を思い切り投げたときの飛距離ほどもある、幅広い大きな橋を作った。トロイアの部隊はその橋をどっと渡り、恐るべきアイギスを掲げたアポロンが先導した。アポロンはアカイア勢の城壁を、海辺で遊ぶ子どもが砂の家を建て、また蹴り倒して壊すのと同じくらい容易に蹴り崩した——まさにそのように、おおアポロンよ、あなたはアルゴス勢に労苦と災いを注ぎ、彼らを恐慌と混乱で満たしたのだ。

units.en: Thus then were the Achaeans hemmed in at their ships, calling out to one another and raising their hands with loud cries every man to heaven. Nestor of Gerene, tower of strength to the Achaeans, lifted up his hands to the starry firmament of heaven, and prayed more fervently than any of them. “Father Jove,” said he, “if ever any one in wheat-growing Argos burned you fat thigh-bones of sheep or heifer and prayed that he might return safely home, whereon you bowed your head to him in assent, bear it in mind now, and suffer not the Trojans to triumph thus over the Achaeans.”
units.ja: こうしてアカイア勢は船のあたりに閉じ込められ、互いに呼び合い、両手を上げて、男たちはそれぞれ大声で天に祈った。ゲレネのネストルは、アカイア勢の力の塔であり、両手を星の輝く天の大空へ差し上げ、誰よりも熱心に祈った。「父ゼウスよ」と彼は言った。「もしこれまでに、麦を産するアルゴスで、誰かが羊や雌牛の太い腿骨をあなたに焼いて捧げ、無事に家へ帰れるようにと祈り、それに対してあなたがうなずいて同意されたことがあるのなら、どうか今それを思い出し、トロイア勢がこのようにアカイア勢に勝ち誇るのをお許しにならないでください。」

notes.title: ネストル
notes.body: ネストルはピュロス王で、ネレウスの子。年老いた知恵者として描かれ、しばしば「アカイア勢の力の塔」と呼ばれる。「ゲレネ」は彼を指す呼び名に添えられた土地の名。
notes.bodyEn: Nestor is king of Pylos and son of Neleus. He is depicted as an aged sage and is often called "tower of strength of the Achaeans." "Gerenian" is a place name attached to the name applied to him.

units.en: All-counselling Jove thundered loudly in answer to the prayer of the aged son of Neleus. When they heard Jove thunder they flung themselves yet more fiercely on the Achaeans. As a wave breaking over the bulwarks of a ship when the sea runs high before a gale—for it is the force of the wind that makes the waves so great—even so did the Trojans spring over the wall with a shout, and drive their chariots onwards. The two sides fought with their double-pointed spears in hand-to-hand encounter-the Trojans from their chariots, and the Achaeans climbing up into their ships and wielding the long pikes that were lying on the decks ready for use in a sea-fight, jointed and shod with bronze.
units.ja: 万知のゼウスは、ネレウスの老いた息子の祈りに応えて、大きく雷鳴をとどろかせた。ゼウスの雷鳴を聞くと、トロイア勢はいっそう激しくアカイア勢へ襲いかかった。嵐の前に海が荒れるとき、波が船の舷側を越えて砕けるように——波をあれほど大きくするのは風の力なのだ——まさにそのように、トロイア勢は叫び声とともに城壁を飛び越え、戦車を進めた。両軍は両端の尖った槍を手にした組み打ちで戦った——トロイア勢は戦車の上から、アカイア勢は船に這い上がり、海上の戦いに備えて甲板に置かれていた、継ぎ目を入れ、青銅で先金をはめた長槍を振るって。

units.en: Now Patroclus, so long as the Achaeans and Trojans were fighting about the wall, but were not yet within it and at the ships, remained sitting in the tent of good Eurypylus, entertaining him with his conversation and spreading herbs over his wound to ease his pain. When, however, he saw the Trojans swarming through the breach in the wall, while the Achaeans were clamouring and struck with panic, he cried aloud, and smote his two thighs with the flat of his hands. “Eurypylus,” said he in his dismay, “I know you want me badly, but I cannot stay with you any longer, for there is hard fighting going on; a servant shall take care of you now, for I must make all speed to Achilles, and induce him to fight if I can; who knows but with heaven’s help I may persuade him. A man does well to listen to the advice of a friend.”
units.ja: さてパトロクロスは、アカイア勢とトロイア勢が城壁のまわりで戦い、まだその内側に入って船のところまで達していなかったあいだは、すぐれたエウリュピュロスの天幕にすわったまま、話し相手になってやり、傷の上に薬草を広げて痛みを和らげていた。しかしトロイア勢が城壁の破れ目からなだれ込むのを見、アカイア勢がどよめき、恐慌に襲われているのを見ると、彼は大声で叫び、両方の腿を手のひらで平手打ちにした。「エウリュピュロス」と彼はうろたえながら言った。「君が私をひどく必要としているのはわかっているが、もうこれ以上君のそばにはいられない。激しい戦いが起きているのだ。あとは従者が君の世話をするだろう。私は急いでアキレウスのもとへ行き、できることなら彼を説得して戦わせねばならない。もしかすると、天の助けがあって、私が彼を説き伏せられるかもしれない。人は友の忠告に耳を貸すのがよいことなのだ。」

notes.title: パトロクロス
notes.body: パトロクロスはアキレウスの最も親しい僚友。ここでは負傷したエウリュピュロスの看病をしながら、戦況の悪化を見てアキレウスのもとへ向かおうとする。
notes.bodyEn: Patroclus is Achilles' closest comrade. Here, while tending the wounded Eurypylus, he sees the worsening state of the battle and makes to head for Achilles.

units.en: When he had thus spoken he went his way. The Achaeans stood firm and resisted the attack of the Trojans, yet though these were fewer in number, they could not drive them back from the ships, neither could the Trojans break the Achaean ranks and make their way in among the tents and ships. As a carpenter’s line gives a true edge to a piece of ship’s timber, in the hand of some skilled workman whom Minerva has instructed in all kinds of useful arts—even so level was the issue of the fight between the two sides, as they fought some round one and some round another.
units.ja: こう言って彼は歩み去った。アカイア勢は踏みとどまり、トロイア勢の攻撃に抗した。しかしトロイア勢は数が少ないにもかかわらず、彼らを船から追い払うこともできず、トロイア勢のほうもアカイア勢の隊列を破って天幕や船のあいだへ入り込むことはできなかった。大工の墨縄が船材に正しい縁をつけるように——アテナがあらゆる役に立つ技を教えた、熟練した職人の手にあるときのように——両軍の戦いの成り行きも、また同じように互角であった。彼らはある者はここをめぐり、ある者はそこをめぐって戦っていた。

units.en: Hector made straight for Ajax, and the two fought fiercely about the same ship. Hector could not force Ajax back and fire the ship, nor yet could Ajax drive Hector from the spot to which heaven had brought him.
units.ja: ヘクトルはまっすぐアイアスに向かい、二人は同じ一そうの船をめぐって激しく戦った。ヘクトルはアイアスを押し返して船に火をかけることはできず、アイアスもまた、天がヘクトルを導き寄せたその場から彼を追い払うことはできなかった。

units.en: Then Ajax struck Caletor son of Clytius in the chest with a spear as he was bringing fire towards the ship. He fell heavily to the ground and the torch dropped from his hand. When Hector saw his cousin fallen in front of the ship he shouted to the Trojans and Lycians saying, “Trojans, Lycians, and Dardanians good in close fight, bate not a jot, but rescue the son of Clytius lest the Achaeans strip him of his armour now that he has fallen.”
units.ja: そのときアイアスは、カレトル——クリュティオスの子——が船へ火を持って来るところを、胸に槍を突き刺した。彼は重く地面に倒れ、松明はその手から落ちた。ヘクトルは、いとこが船の前で倒れるのを見ると、トロイア勢とリュキア勢に叫んで言った。「トロイア勢、リュキア勢、そして近接戦に強いダルダノス勢よ、少しも緩めるな。クリュティオスの子を救い出せ。彼が倒れた今、アカイア勢に武具を剥ぎ取られてはならぬ。」

units.en: He then aimed a spear at Ajax, and missed him, but he hit Lycophron a follower of Ajax, who came from Cythera, but was living with Ajax inasmuch as he had killed a man among the Cythereans. Hector’s spear struck him on the head below the ear, and he fell headlong from the ship’s prow on to the ground with no life left in him. Ajax shook with rage and said to his brother, “Teucer, my good fellow, our trusty comrade the son of Mastor has fallen, he came to live with us from Cythera and whom we honoured as much as our own parents. Hector has just killed him; fetch your deadly arrows at once and the bow which Phoebus Apollo gave you.”
units.ja: 彼は次にアイアスに槍を狙い定めて投げたが、外れ、代わりにアイアスの従者リュコプロンに当たった。キュテラの出だが、キュテラの人々のあいだで一人を殺したため、アイアスのもとに身を寄せて暮らしていた。ヘクトルの槍は彼の頭の耳の下を打ち、彼は船の舳先から真っ逆さまに地面へ落ち、息の根は絶えていた。アイアスは怒りに身を震わせ、弟に言った。「テウクロス、わが友よ、われらの信頼する僚友、マストルの子が倒れた。彼はキュテラからわれらのもとへ来て暮らし、われらは実の親と同じほどに彼を敬っていた。ヘクトルが今しがた彼を殺したのだ。すぐに、お前の殺す矢と、ポイボス・アポロンがお前に与えた弓を持って来い。」

notes.title: テウクロス
notes.body: テウクロスはアイアスの異母兄弟で、弓の名手。ここでアイアスは、倒された僚友リュコプロンの復讐のために彼へ弓を取って来るよう命じる。
notes.bodyEn: Teucer is Ajax's half-brother and a master archer. Here Ajax orders him to fetch his bow in order to avenge their fallen comrade Lycophron.

units.en: Teucer heard him and hastened towards him with his bow and quiver in his hands. Forthwith he showered his arrows on the Trojans, and hit Cleitus the son of Pisenor, comrade of Polydamas the noble son of Panthous, with the reins in his hands as he was attending to his horses; he was in the middle of the very thickest part of the fight, doing good service to Hector and the Trojans, but evil had now come upon him, and not one of those who were fain to do so could avert it, for the arrow struck him on the back of the neck. He fell from his chariot and his horses shook the empty car as they swerved aside. King Polydamas saw what had happened, and was the first to come up to the horses; he gave them in charge to Astynous son of Protiaon, and ordered him to look on, and to keep the horses near at hand. He then went back and took his place in the front ranks.
units.ja: テウクロスはその声を聞くと、弓と矢筒を手にして急ぎ足で彼のもとへ向かった。たちまち彼はトロイア勢に矢を雨と降らせ、手綱を手にして馬の世話をしていたピセノルの子クレイトスに命中させた。クレイトスは、パントオスの子で高貴なポリュダマスの従者であった。彼は戦いのまさに最も密集した中心にあって、ヘクトルとトロイア勢によく尽くしていたが、今や災いが彼に降りかかり、そう望む者のうちの誰一人としてそれを避けさせることはできなかった。矢は彼の首の後ろに突き刺さったからである。彼は戦車から落ち、馬は横にそれながら、もぬけの殻となった車を揺さぶった。王ポリュダマスは事の次第を見て取り、真っ先に馬たちのもとへ駆け寄った。彼は馬をプロティアオンの子アステュノオスに託し、見張りをして、馬を手近に保っておくよう命じた。それから彼は引き返し、前線の列にその身を置いた。

notes.title: テウクロス
notes.body: サラミス島の弓の名手で、テラモンの子アイアス（大アイアス）の異母弟。この場面では弓射によってトロイア勢を攻め立てています。
notes.bodyEn: An archer of Salamis and the half-brother of Ajax, son of Telamon (Great Ajax). In this scene he is pressing the Trojans hard with his archery.

units.en: Teucer then aimed another arrow at Hector, and there would have been no more fighting at the ships if he had hit him and killed him then and there: Jove, however, who kept watch over Hector, had his eyes on Teucer, and deprived him of his triumph, by breaking his bowstring for him just as he was drawing it and about to take his aim; on this the arrow went astray and the bow fell from his hands. Teucer shook with anger and said to his brother, “Alas, see how heaven thwarts us in all we do; it has broken my bowstring and snatched the bow from my hand, though I strung it this self-same morning that it might serve me for many an arrow.”
units.ja: 次にテウクロスはヘクトルへもう一本の矢を向けた。もしそこで彼に当てて殺していたなら、船のあたりでこれ以上の戦いはなかったであろう。しかしヘクトルを見守るゼウスはテウクロスから目を離さず、彼が弓を引き絞り、まさに狙いを定めようとしたそのときに弓弦を断ち切って、彼から勝利を奪い去った。そこで矢はそれて飛び、弓は彼の手から落ちた。テウクロスは怒りに震えて兄に言った。「ああ、ごらんください、天はわれらのなすことごとにこうも妨げに入るのです。私の弓弦を断ち切り、弓を私の手から奪い去りました。今朝つい先ほど、数多くの矢を射るために張ったばかりだというのに。」

notes.title: ヘクトルを見守るゼウス
notes.body: ゼウスがヘクトルを特に見守り、弓弦を断ってテウクロスの射を妨げる場面です。神の意志が戦況を直接左右するという、この叙事詩に典型的な構図を示しています。
notes.bodyEn: This is the scene in which Zeus watches over Hector in particular and breaks the bowstring to thwart Teucer's shot. It shows the pattern typical of this epic, in which the will of a god directly determines the course of the battle.

units.en: Ajax son of Telamon answered, “My good fellow, let your bow and your arrows be, for Jove has made them useless in order to spite the Danaans. Take your spear, lay your shield upon your shoulder, and both fight the Trojans yourself and urge others to do so. They may be successful for the moment but if we fight as we ought they will find it a hard matter to take the ships.”
units.ja: テラモンの子アイアスが答えた。「わが友よ、弓と矢のことは捨て置け。ゼウスがダナオイ勢を困らせようとして、それらを役立たずにしてしまったのだ。槍を取れ、盾を肩に載せよ。そして自分でもトロイア勢と戦い、他の者たちにもそうするよう勧めよ。奴らは今しばらくはうまく運ぶかもしれぬが、われらがなすべきように戦うならば、船を奪うのは奴らにとって難儀なこととなろう。」

notes.title: ダナオイ勢・アルゴス勢
notes.body: ギリシア勢はアカイア勢のほかに、ダナオイ勢（ダナオスの子孫）、アルゴス勢（アルゴスの人々）とも呼ばれ、いずれも同じ集団を指します。ここでは原文の呼び分けをそのまま訳し分けています。
notes.bodyEn: Besides Achaeans, the Greek army is also called Danaans (descendants of Danaus) and Argives (people of Argos), and all of these refer to the same group. Here the different designations in the source text are rendered with different words just as they are.

units.en: Teucer then took his bow and put it by in his tent. He hung a shield four hides thick about his shoulders, and on his comely head he set his helmet well wrought with a crest of horse-hair that nodded menacingly above it; he grasped his redoubtable bronze-shod spear, and forthwith he was by the side of Ajax.
units.ja: そこでテウクロスは弓を取り、自分の天幕にしまった。彼は四枚の牛皮の厚さの盾を肩にかけ、見目のよい頭には、馬の尾毛の冠をつけた、その上で威嚇するように揺れる、よく鍛えられた兜をかぶった。彼は恐るべき青銅の石突きの槍を握り、たちまちアイアスの傍らに並んだ。

units.en: When Hector saw that Teucer’s bow was of no more use to him, he shouted out to the Trojans and Lycians, “Trojans, Lycians, and Dardanians good in close fight, be men, my friends, and show your mettle here at the ships, for I see the weapon of one of their chieftains made useless by the hand of Jove. It is easy to see when Jove is helping people and means to help them still further, or again when he is bringing them down and will do nothing for them; he is now on our side, and is going against the Argives. Therefore swarm round the ships and fight. If any of you is struck by spear or sword and loses his life, let him die; he dies with honour who dies fighting for his country; and he will leave his wife and children safe behind him, with his house and allotment unplundered if only the Achaeans can be driven back to their own land, they and their ships.”
units.ja: ヘクトルは、テウクロスの弓がもはや彼にとって役に立たぬと見て取ると、トロイア勢とリュキア勢に向かって叫んだ。「トロイア勢、リュキア勢、そして近接戦に強いダルダノス勢よ、友らよ、男らしくあれ、この船のあたりで力を示せ。彼らの将の一人の武器がゼウスの手によって役立たずにされたのを、この目で見たからだ。ゼウスが人々を助け、さらに助けようとしているのか、それとも彼らを打ち倒し、何もしてやろうとしないのかは、容易に見て取れる。今やゼウスはわれらに味方し、アルゴス勢に逆らっている。ゆえに船の周りに群がって戦え。もしお前たちのうちの誰かが槍や剣に打たれて命を失うなら、死ぬがよい。国のために戦って死ぬ者は名誉のうちに死ぬ。そしてアカイア勢を、彼らとその船とともに自らの国へ追い返すことができさえすれば、その者は妻と子を、家と割当地を奪われることなく無事に後に残すであろう。」

units.en: With these words he put heart and soul into them all. Ajax on the other side exhorted his comrades saying, “Shame on you Argives, we are now utterly undone, unless we can save ourselves by driving the enemy from our ships. Do you think, if Hector takes them, that you will be able to get home by land? Can you not hear him cheering on his whole host to fire our fleet, and bidding them remember that they are not at a dance but in battle? Our only course is to fight them with might and main; we had better chance it, life or death, once for all, than fight long and without issue hemmed in at our ships by worse men than ourselves.”
units.ja: こう言って彼は皆の心に命と魂を吹き込んだ。その一方、アイアスは仲間たちに呼びかけて言った。「アルゴス勢よ、恥を知れ。今やわれらは、敵を船から追い払って自らを救わぬ限り、まったくの破滅である。もしヘクトルが船を奪ったなら、お前たちは陸路で帰国できると思うのか。奴が全軍にわれらの船団へ火をかけよと励まし、自分たちは踊りの場におらず戦いのさなかにいるのだと心に刻めと命じているのが、聞こえぬのか。われらの道はただ一つ、力の限りを尽くして奴らと戦うことだ。自分たちより劣った者たちに船のところで囲まれて、長々と実りのない戦いを続けるより、一度きり、生か死かを賭けるほうがましである。」

units.en: With these words he put life and soul into them all. Hector then killed Schedius son of Perimedes, leader of the Phoceans, and Ajax killed Laodamas captain of foot soldiers and son to Antenor. Polydamas killed Otus of Cyllene a comrade of the son of Phyleus and chief of the proud Epeans. When Meges saw this he sprang upon him, but Polydamas crouched down, and he missed him, for Apollo would not suffer the son of Panthous to fall in battle; but the spear hit Croesmus in the middle of his chest, whereon he fell heavily to the ground, and Meges stripped him of his armour. At that moment the valiant soldier Dolops son of Lampus sprang upon Lampus was son of Laomedon and noted for his valour, while his son Dolops was versed in all the ways of war. He then struck the middle of the son of Phyleus’ shield with his spear, setting on him at close quarters, but his good corslet made with plates of metal saved him; Phyleus had brought it from Ephyra and the river Selleis, where his host, King Euphetes, had given it him to wear in battle and protect him. It now served to save the life of his son. Then Meges struck the topmost crest of Dolops’s bronze helmet with his spear and tore away its plume of horse-hair, so that all newly dyed with scarlet as it was it tumbled down into the dust. While he was still fighting and confident of victory, Menelaus came up to help Meges, and got by the side of Dolops unperceived; he then speared him in the shoulder, from behind, and the point, driven so furiously, went through into his chest, whereon he fell headlong. The two then made towards him to strip him of his armour, but Hector called on all his brothers for help, and he especially upbraided brave Melanippus son of Hiketaon, who erewhile used to pasture his herds of cattle in Percote before the war broke out; but when the ships of the Danaans came, he went back to Ilius, where he was eminent among the Trojans, and lived near Priam who treated him as one of his own sons. Hector now rebuked him and said, “Why, Melanippus, are we thus remiss? do you take no note of the death of your kinsman, and do you not see how they are trying to take Dolops’s armour? Follow me; there must be no fighting the Argives from a distance now, but we must do so in close combat till either we kill them or they take the high wall of Ilius and slay her people.”
units.ja: こう言って彼は皆に生気と魂を吹き込んだ。次いでヘクトルは、ポキス勢の将ペリメデスの子スケディオスを殺し、アイアスは歩兵の将でアンテノルの子ラオダマスを殺した。ポリュダマスは、キュレネのオトスを殺した。オトスはフィレウスの子の従者で、誇り高きエペイオイ勢の長であった。メゲスはこれを見てポリュダマスに跳びかかったが、ポリュダマスは身をかがめたので、彼は外した。アポロンがパントオスの子を戦場で倒れさせようとはしなかったからである。しかし槍はクロイスモスの胸の真ん中に当たり、彼はそのまま重く地面に倒れ、メゲスは彼の武具を剥ぎ取った。そのとき、勇ましい戦士ラムポスの子ドロプスが跳びかかった。ラムポスはラオメドンの子で武勇に名高く、その子ドロプスはあらゆる戦いの道に通じていた。彼はフィレウスの子の盾の真ん中を槍で突き、間近から襲いかかったが、その子の見事な金属板作りの胸甲が彼を救った。フィレウスはそれをエピュラとセレイス川のほとりから持ち帰ったもので、そこでは彼の主人である王エウフェテスが、戦いで身につけて我が身を守るようにと彼に与えたのだった。今それは彼の子の命を救う役目を果たした。そこでメゲスは、ドロプスの青銅の兜のいちばん上の峰を槍で突き、馬毛の飾り房を引きちぎったので、真紅に染めたばかりのそれは塵の中に落ちた。彼がなおも戦い、勝利を確信していたとき、メネラオスがメゲスを助けにやって来て、ドロプスの傍らに気づかれずに近づいた。彼は後ろから彼の肩を槍で突き、その穂先は猛烈に突き進んで胸まで達し、彼はそのまま真っ逆さまに倒れた。二人は彼に近づいて武具を剥ぎ取ろうとしたが、ヘクトルはすべての兄弟たちに助けを求め、とりわけ勇ましいヒュケタオンの子メラニッポスをとがめた。この者は戦が起こる前にはペルコテで牛の群れを放牧していたが、ダナオイ勢の船がやって来るとイリオスへ戻り、そこでトロイア勢の間で重んじられ、我が子の一人のように遇するプリアモスの近くに住んでいた。ヘクトルは彼を責めて言った。「どうしたことか、メラニッポス、われらはこうも手ぬるいのか。自分の親族が死んだことに気づかぬのか、奴らがドロプスの武具を奪おうとしているのが見えぬのか。我に続け。もうアルゴス勢と遠くから戦ってはならぬ。われらが奴らを殺すか、奴らがイリオスの高い城壁を奪ってその民を殺すか、そのどちらかになるまで、近接戦で戦わねばならぬ。」

notes.title: 語の重なった一文
notes.body: ドロプスの登場する一文は、与えられた英文では語が重複して文が乱れており、「勇ましい戦士ラムポスの子ドロプスが跳びかかった」と読むのが自然です。この箇所の原文の文意には解釈の余地があります。
notes.bodyEn: In the English text as given, the sentence in which Drops appears has duplicated words and is garbled, and it reads most naturally as "the valiant warrior Drops, son of Lampus, sprang forward." There is room for interpretation as to what the original text means at this point.

units.en: He led on as he spoke, and the hero Melanippus followed after. Meanwhile Ajax son of Telamon was cheering on the Argives. “My friends,” he cried, “be men, and fear dishonour; quit yourselves in battle so as to win respect from one another. Men who respect each other’s good opinion are less likely to be killed than those who do not, but in flight there is neither gain nor glory.”
units.ja: 彼はそう言いながら先頭に立って進み、勇者メラニッポスが後について行った。その間、テラモンの子アイアスはアルゴス勢を励ましていた。「友らよ」と彼は叫んだ。「男らしくあれ、不名誉を恐れよ。互いに敬意を得られるように戦いに励め。互いの良い評価を重んじる者たちは、そうでない者たちよりも殺されることが少ない。だが逃げることには利も栄光もない。」

units.en: Thus did he exhort men who were already bent upon driving back the Trojans. They laid his words to heart and hedged the ships as with a wall of bronze, while Jove urged on the Trojans. Menelaus of the loud battle-cry urged Antilochus on. “Antilochus,” said he, “you are young and there is none of the Achaeans more fleet of foot or more valiant than you are. See if you cannot spring upon some Trojan and kill him.”
units.ja: こうして彼は、すでにトロイア勢を押し返そうと心を決めている者たちを励ました。彼らはその言葉を心に刻み、あたかも青銅の壁のように船を囲んだ。一方、ゼウスはトロイア勢を駆り立てていた。雄叫び高きメネラオスはアンティロコスを励ました。「アンティロコス」と彼は言った。「お前は若く、アカイア勢のうちでお前より足の速い者も、お前より勇ましい者もいない。トロイア勢の誰かに跳びかかって殺せはしないか、やってみよ。」

notes.title: アンティロコス
notes.body: 老将ネストルの子で、若く足の速い戦士として描かれます。
notes.bodyEn: The son of the aged commander Nestor, depicted as a young and swift-footed warrior.

units.en: He hurried away when he had thus spurred Antilochus, who at once darted out from the front ranks and aimed a spear, after looking carefully round him. The Trojans fell back as he threw, and the dart did not speed from his hand without effect, for it struck Melanippus the proud son of Hiketaon in the breast by the nipple as he was coming forward, and his armour rang rattling round him as he fell heavily to the ground. Antilochus sprang upon him as a dog springs on a fawn which a hunter has hit as it was breaking away from its covert, and killed it. Even so, O Melanippus, did stalwart Antilochus spring upon you to strip you of your armour; but noble Hector marked him, and came running up to him through the thick of the battle. Antilochus, brave soldier though he was, would not stay to face him, but fled like some savage creature which knows it has done wrong, and flies, when it has killed a dog or a man who is herding his cattle, before a body of men can be gathered to attack it. Even so did the son of Nestor fly, and the Trojans and Hector with a cry that rent the air showered their weapons after him; nor did he turn round and stay his flight till he had reached his comrades.
units.ja: こうしてアンティロコスを励ましたうえで、彼は急ぎ去った。アンティロコスはただちに前列から飛び出し、あたりを入念に見回してから槍をねらった。彼が投げるとトロイア勢は後じさりし、その投枪はむなしく手を離れたのではなかった。進み出てきたヒュペタオンの子、誇り高きメラニッポスの胸、乳首のあたりを射貫いたので、彼がどうと倒れると、武具が周囲でがらがらと鳴り響いた。アンティロコスは、獲物が物陰から飛び出したところを猟師に撃たれた鹿の子に犬が跳びかかるように、彼の上に跳びかかってとどめを刺した。まさにそのように、おおメラニッポスよ、勇壮なアンティロコスはあなたから武具をはぎ取ろうと跳びかかった。しかし高貴なヘクトルはそれに気づき、乱戦のただ中を走り寄ってきた。アンティロコスは勇敢な戦士ではあったが、彼と向き合ってとどまろうとはせず、自分が悪いことをしたと知っている野獣のように逃げた。犬か、牛の群れを追う男を殺してしまった獣が、人々が群れをなして襲ってくる前に逃げ去る、あの姿である。まさにそのようにネストルの子は逃げた。トロイア勢とヘクトルは空を裂く叫びをあげて彼の後へ武具を浴びせかけたが、彼は味方のもとにたどり着くまで振り返りもせず、逃走をやめもしなかった。

notes.title: アンティロコス
notes.body: アカイア勢の戦士で、老将ネストルの子。父とともに戦場にある若武者として描かれ、この場面では投枪でトロイア勢のメラニッポスを倒します。
notes.bodyEn: An Achaean warrior and the son of the aged commander Nestor. He is depicted as a young fighter on the battlefield alongside his father, and in this scene he fells Melanippus of the Trojans with a thrown spear.

units.en: The Trojans, fierce as lions, were still rushing on towards the ships in fulfilment of the behests of Jove who kept spurring them on to new deeds of daring, while he deadened the courage of the Argives and defeated them by encouraging the Trojans. For he meant giving glory to Hector son of Priam, and letting him throw fire upon the ships, till he had fulfilled the unrighteous prayer that Thetis had made him; Jove, therefore, bided his time till he should see the glare of a blazing ship. From that hour he was about so to order that the Trojans should be driven back from the ships and to vouchsafe glory to the Achaeans. With this purpose he inspired Hector son of Priam, who was eager enough already, to assail the ships. His fury was as that of Mars, or as when a fire is raging in the glades of some dense forest upon the mountains; he foamed at the mouth, his eyes glared under his terrible eyebrows, and his helmet quivered on his temples by reason of the fury with which he fought. Jove from heaven was with him, and though he was but one against many, vouchsafed him victory and glory; for he was doomed to an early death, and already Pallas Minerva was hurrying on the hour of his destruction at the hands of the son of Peleus. Now, however, he kept trying to break the ranks of the enemy wherever he could see them thickest, and in the goodliest armour; but do what he might he could not break through them, for they stood as a tower foursquare, or as some high cliff rising from the grey sea that braves the anger of the gale, and of the waves that thunder up against it. He fell upon them like flames of fire from every quarter. As when a wave, raised mountain high by wind and storm, breaks over a ship and covers it deep in foam, the fierce winds roar against the mast, the hearts of the sailors fail them for fear, and they are saved but by a very little from destruction—even so were the hearts of the Achaeans fainting within them. Or as a savage lion attacking a herd of cows while they are feeding by thousands in the low-lying meadows by some wide-watered shore—the herdsman is at his wit’s end how to protect his herd and keeps going about now in the van and now in the rear of his cattle, while the lion springs into the thick of them and fastens on a cow so that they all tremble for fear—even so were the Achaeans utterly panic-stricken by Hector and father Jove. Nevertheless Hector only killed Periphetes of Mycenae; he was son of Copreus who was wont to take the orders of King Eurystheus to mighty Hercules, but the son was a far better man than the father in every way; he was fleet of foot, a valiant warrior, and in understanding ranked among the foremost men of Mycenae. He it was who then afforded Hector a triumph, for as he was turning back he stumbled against the rim of his shield which reached his feet, and served to keep the javelins off him. He tripped against this and fell face upward, his helmet ringing loudly about his head as he did so. Hector saw him fall and ran up to him; he then thrust a spear into his chest, and killed him close to his own comrades. These, for all their sorrow, could not help him for they were themselves terribly afraid of Hector.
units.ja: 獅子のように猛るトロイア勢は、ゼウスの命を果たそうと、なおも船めがけて突き進んでいた。ゼウスは彼らを新たな勇気の行いへと駆り立て続ける一方、アルゴス勢の勇気を鈍らせ、トロイア勢を励ますことで彼らを打ち破っていた。というのもゼウスは、プリアモスの子ヘクトルに栄光を与え、テティスが彼にした不義の願いを果たし終えるまで、彼に船へ火を放たせようとしていたからである。それゆえゼウスは、燃えさかる船の輝きを見るまで時を待った。その時から彼は、トロイア勢を船から撃退し、アカイア勢に栄光を授けるよう計らうつもりでいた。その意図をもって、彼はもとから十分に意欲的なプリアモスの子ヘクトルを、船に襲いかかるよう奮い立たせた。彼の怒りはアレスにも似、あるいは山の上、深い森の木立に火が燃えさかるときのようであった。彼は口に泡を吹き、恐ろしい眉の下で目はぎらつき、戦いの激しさのゆえに兜はこめかみの上で揺れた。天からゼウスが彼とともにあり、彼は一人で多勢を相手にしながらも勝利と栄光を授けられた。彼は早い死を定められており、すでにパラス・アテナは、ペレウスの子の手による滅びの時を急がせていたのである。しかしこの時、彼は敵の隊列が最も密なところ、最も見事な武具のところを見定めては、それを破ろうと努め続けた。だがどう努めても突き破れなかった。彼らは四角い塔のように、あるいは灰色の海からそびえ立つ高い崖のように、嵐の怒りや、それに轟きかかる波に立ち向かって立っていたからである。彼は四方から炎のように彼らに襲いかかった。風と嵐によって山のように高く巻き上げられた波が船を越えて打ちかかり、船を深く泡で覆うとき、激しい風は帆柱に向かって吠え、水夫たちの心は恐れに挫け、彼らはごくわずかの差で破滅を免れる——まさにそのように、アカイア勢の心は内側で挫けていた。あるいは、荒々しい獅子が、広い水辺の低い草地で数千頭と群れなして草を食む牛の群れを襲うとき——牛飼いは群れをどう守ればよいか途方に暮れ、牛の前を行き後ろを行きしながら歩き回るが、獅子は群れの真ん中へ跳び込み、一頭の牛に食らいつくので、牛たちは皆おののく——まさにそのように、アカイア勢はヘクトルと父ゼウスによってすっかり恐慌に陥っていた。それでもヘクトルが殺したのは、ミュケナイのペリペテスただ一人であった。彼は、王エウリュステウスから力あるヘラクレスへ命令を伝える役目をしていたコプレウスの子であったが、その子はあらゆる点で父よりはるかに優れた男であった。足が速く、勇ましい戦士で、理解力においてもミュケナイの一流の男たちの中に数えられた。ヘクトルに勝利を授けたのはこの男であった。というのも、彼は後ろへ向き直ったとき、足元まで届いて投枪を防いでいた自分の盾の縁につまずいたのである。彼はこれにつまずいて仰向けに倒れ、そのとき兜は頭の周りで大きく鳴り響いた。ヘクトルは彼が倒れるのを見て走り寄り、その胸に槍を突き立て、彼自身の味方のすぐそばで彼を殺した。味方たちは悲しみながらも彼を助けることはできなかった。彼ら自身、ヘクトルをひどく恐れていたからである。

notes.title: テティス
notes.body: 海の女神で、アキレウスの母。ゼウスに、アカイア勢が敗れるよう願ったとされ、本文ではそれを「不義の願い」と呼びます。
notes.bodyEn: A sea goddess and the mother of Achilles. She is said to have prayed to Zeus that the Achaeans be defeated, and the text calls this an "unrighteous prayer."

units.en: They had now reached the ships and the prows of those that had been drawn up first were on every side of them, but the Trojans came pouring after them. The Argives were driven back from the first row of ships, but they made a stand by their tents without being broken up and scattered; shame and fear restrained them. They kept shouting incessantly to one another, and Nestor of Gerene, tower of strength to the Achaeans, was loudest in imploring every man by his parents, and beseeching him to stand firm.
units.ja: 彼らは今や船にたどり着いていた。先に引き揚げられた船の舳先が四方に迫るなか、トロイア勢は後を追ってなだれ込んできた。アルゴス勢は第一列の船から押し戻されたが、崩れて散り散りになることなく、天幕のそばで踏みとどまった。恥と恐れが彼らを引き止めたのである。彼らは絶え間なく互いに呼びかけ合い、アカイア勢の力の塔であるゲレネのネストルは、誰よりも声高に、皆に父母の名にかけて懇願し、踏みとどまるよう切に求めた。

units.en: “Be men, my friends,” he cried, “and respect one another’s good opinion. Think, all of you, on your children, your wives, your property, and your parents whether these be alive or dead. On their behalf though they are not here, I implore you to stand firm, and not to turn in flight.”
units.ja: 「男らしくあれ、友よ」と彼は叫んだ。「そして互いの良い評判を重んじよ。皆、よく考えよ、自分の子ら、妻、財産、そして父母のことを——それが生きていようと死んでいようと。彼らのために、彼らがここにいないとしても、私はあなた方に、踏みとどまり、逃げて背を向けぬよう懇願する。」

units.en: With these words he put heart and soul into them all. Minerva lifted the thick veil of darkness from their eyes, and much light fell upon them, alike on the side of the ships and on that where the fight was raging. They could see Hector and all his men, both those in the rear who were taking no part in the battle, and those who were fighting by the ships.
units.ja: これらの言葉によって、彼は皆に心と魂を吹き込んだ。アテナは彼らの目から濃い闇の覆いを取り去り、船のある側でも、戦いが激しく行われている側でも、それらに多くの光が降り注いだ。彼らはヘクトルとその部下すべてを、戦いに加わらず後方にいる者たちも、船のそばで戦っている者たちも、見分けることができた。

notes.title: パラス・アテナ
notes.body: 知恵と戦いを司る女神で、アカイア勢の守り手。ここでは彼らの目を覆っていた闇を取り去り、戦場を見渡せるようにします。味方に働く神の力が際立つ場面です。
notes.bodyEn: The goddess who governs wisdom and war, and the protector of the Achaeans. Here she removes the darkness that covered their eyes so that they can look out over the battlefield. It is a scene in which the power of a god working on behalf of her own side stands out.

units.en: Ajax could not bring himself to retreat along with the rest, but strode from deck to deck with a great sea-pike in his hands twelve cubits long and jointed with rings. As a man skilled in feats of horsemanship couples four horses together and comes tearing full speed along the public way from the country into some large town—many both men and women marvel as they see him for he keeps all the time changing his horse, springing from one to another without ever missing his feet while the horses are at a gallop—even so did Ajax go striding from one ship’s deck to another, and his voice went up into the heavens. He kept on shouting his orders to the Danaans and exhorting them to defend their ships and tents; neither did Hector remain within the main body of the Trojan warriors, but as a dun eagle swoops down upon a flock of wild-fowl feeding near a river—geese, it may be, or cranes, or long-necked swans—even so did Hector make straight for a dark-prowed ship, rushing right towards it; for Jove with his mighty hand impelled him forward, and roused his people to follow him.
units.ja: アイアスは他の者たちとともに退く気にはなれず、十二キュビトの長さで環でつながれた大きな船ざおを両手に持ち、甲板から甲板へと大股に歩き回った。馬術の技に長けた男が四頭の馬を一つに組み、街道を国から大きな町へと全速力で駆け抜けるとき、彼が絶えず馬を乗り換え、疾走する馬から馬へと足を踏み外すことなく飛び移るのを、多くの男女が驚いて見守る——まさにそのように、アイアスは船の甲板から甲板へと大股に進み、その声は天へと届いた。彼はダナオス勢に命令を叫び続け、船と天幕を守るよう励ました。ヘクトルもまたトロイア勢の本隊にとどまらず、くすんだ色の鷲が川辺で餌をあさる水鳥の群れ——雁か、鶴か、あるいは首の長い白鳥か——に舞い降りるように、まっすぐに黒い舳先の船へと突き進んだ。ゼウスが力強い手で彼を前へ押し進め、民を彼に従わせるよう奮い立たせていたからである。

notes.title: キュビト
notes.body: ひじから中指の先までの長さを基準にした古代の単位。十二キュビトは五メートルを超える長さにあたり、船をめぐる戦いで用いる長いさおを表します。
notes.bodyEn: An ancient unit of length based on the distance from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger. Twelve cubits amount to a length of more than five meters, and here it describes the long pole used in the fighting around the ships.

units.en: And now the battle again raged furiously at the ships. You would have thought the men were coming on fresh and unwearied, so fiercely did they fight; and this was the mind in which they were—the Achaeans did not believe they should escape destruction but thought themselves doomed, while there was not a Trojan but his heart beat high with the hope of firing the ships and putting the Achaean heroes to the sword.
units.ja: そして今や、戦いは再び船のそばで激しく燃えあがった。兵たちが新たに、疲れを知らぬ者として襲いかかってくるとでも思われるほど、激しく戦った。そしてこれが彼らの心のありようであった——アカイア勢は自分たちが滅びを免れるとは信じておらず、自分たちは死すべき運命にあると思っていた。一方、船に火を放ち、アカイアの勇者たちを剣にかけようとの望みに胸を高鳴らせないトロイア人は一人もいなかった。

units.en: Thus were the two sides minded. Then Hector seized the stern of the good ship that had brought Protesilaus to Troy, but never bore him back to his native land. Round this ship there raged a close hand-to-hand fight between Danaans and Trojans. They did not fight at a distance with bows and javelins, but with one mind hacked at one another in close combat with their mighty swords and spears pointed at both ends; they fought moreover with keen battle-axes and with hatchets. Many a good stout blade hilted and scabbarded with iron, fell from hand or shoulder as they fought, and the earth ran red with blood. Hector, when he had seized the ship, would not loose his hold but held on to its curved stern and shouted to the Trojans, “Bring fire, and raise the battle-cry all of you with a single voice. Now has Jove vouchsafed us a day that will pay us for all the rest; this day we shall take the ships which came hither against heaven’s will, and which have caused us such infinite suffering through the cowardice of our councillors, who when I would have done battle at the ships held me back and forbade the host to follow me; if Jove did then indeed warp our judgements, himself now commands me and cheers me on.”
units.ja: 両軍の将士はかくのごとき心づもりであった。そこへヘクトルが、プロテシラオスをトロイアへ運びはしたものの、二度と彼を故国へ連れ戻すことのなかったあの立派な船の船尾をつかんだ。この船をめぐって、ダナオス勢とトロイア勢の間で、肩と肩が触れ合うほどの近接戦が燃えさかった。彼らは弓や投げ槍で遠くから戦うのではなく、一心に、力強い剣や両端に穂をつけた槍を手に、入り乱れて斬り合った。さらに彼らはよく研いだ戦斧や手斧でも戦った。鉄の柄と鉄の鞘を備えた、頑丈で立派な刃が幾つも、戦ううちに手から、あるいは肩から落ち、大地は血で赤く染まった。ヘクトルは船をつかむと、その手を緩めようとせず、湾曲した船尾にしがみついてトロイア勢に叫んだ。「火を持ってこい。そしてお前たち全員、声を一つにして鬨の声を上げよ。今こそゼウスは、これまでのすべてを償わせてくれる一日を我らに授けてくださった。この日に我らは、天の意に逆らってここへ来た船、すなわち、評議の者たちの臆病さゆえに我らに限りない苦しみをもたらした船を、奪い取るのだ。あの者たちは、私が船のそばで戦おうとしたとき、私を引き止め、軍勢が私に続くのを禁じた。もしゼウスがそのとき確かに我らの判断を歪めておられたのだとしても、今はゼウスご自身が私に命じ、私を励ましておられるのだ。」

notes.title: プロテシラオス
notes.body: トロイア戦争に加わったギリシア側の武将で、トロイアの岸に最初に上陸し、その直後にヘクトルに討たれたと伝えられる。「船は彼を故国へ連れ戻さなかった」という一節は、彼が帰還を果たせなかったことを指す。
notes.bodyEn: A Greek commander who took part in the Trojan War; he is said to have been the first to land on the shore of Troy and to have been killed by Hector immediately afterward. The phrase "the ship did not carry him back to his homeland" refers to his failure to return home.

units.en: As he spoke thus the Trojans sprang yet more fiercely on the Achaeans, and Ajax no longer held his ground, for he was overcome by the darts that were flung at him, and made sure that he was doomed. Therefore he left the raised deck at the stern, and stepped back on to the seven-foot bench of the oarsmen. Here he stood on the look-out, and with his spear held back any Trojan whom he saw bringing fire to the ships. All the time he kept on shouting at the top of his voice and exhorting the Danaans. “My friends,” he cried, “Danaan heroes, servants of Mars, be men my friends, and fight with might and with main. Can we hope to find helpers hereafter, or a wall to shield us more surely than the one we have? There is no strong city within reach, whence we may draw fresh forces to turn the scales in our favour. We are on the plain of the armed Trojans with the sea behind us, and far from our own country. Our salvation, therefore, is in the might of our hands and in hard fighting.”
units.ja: 彼がこう語るやいなや、トロイア勢はいっそう激しくアカイア勢に襲いかかった。アイアスはもはや持ち場を守りきれなかった。彼に投げつけられる投槍に打ち負かされ、自分は死ぬ運命にあると確信したからである。そこで彼は船尾の張り出した甲板を離れ、櫂手たちが使う七フィートの腰掛けへと後退した。ここに立って見張りをし、船へ火を運ぼうとするトロイア勢を見つけては、槍を構えて追い払った。その間ずっと、彼は声の限りに叫び、ダナオス勢を励まし続けた。「友よ」と彼は叫んだ。「ダナオスの勇士たち、アレスの従者たちよ、友よ、男らしくあれ、力の限り、全身全霊で戦え。これから先、われらを助けてくれる者を見つけられるだろうか。われらが今持っているこの砦よりも確かな盾となってくれる壁を見つけられるだろうか。形勢をわれらに有利に傾けるための新しい軍勢を引き出せるほどの、手の届くところに堅固な都はない。われらは武装したトロイア勢の平野にあり、背には海があり、故国から遠く離れている。ゆえにわれらの救いは、この両腕の力と、苛烈な戦いにあるのだ。」

notes.title: ダナオス勢とアカイア勢
notes.body: 「ダナオス勢」はアカイア勢と同じギリシア側の軍勢を指す別名で、伝説上の祖ダナオスに由来する。本訳では Acaeans に「アカイア勢」を当てているが、原文が Danaans と記す箇所はその別名として「ダナオス勢」とした。
notes.bodyEn: "The Danaans" is an alternative name for the same Greek forces as the Achaeans, deriving from the legendary ancestor Danaus. In this translation "Acaeans" is used for the Achaeans, but where the original text writes "Danaans" this is given as the alternative name "the Danaans."

units.en: As he spoke he wielded his spear with still greater fury, and when any Trojan made towards the ships with fire at Hector’s bidding, he would be on the look-out for him, and drive at him with his long spear. Twelve men did he thus kill in hand-to-hand fight before the ships.
units.ja: 彼はこう語りながら、いっそう激しく槍を振るった。ヘクトルの命を受けて火を手に船へ向かうトロイア勢があれば、彼はそれを見張っていて、長い槍で突きかかった。こうして彼は、船の前での近接戦で十二人を討ち取った。

notes.title: 大アイアス
notes.body: サラミス島の王テラモンの子で、「大アイアス」と呼ばれる。ギリシア勢きっての守りの武将であり、この場面では船を守る要となって踏みとどまっている。
notes.bodyEn: The son of Telamon, king of Salamis, and called "Great Ajax." He is the foremost defensive warrior of the Greek forces, and in this scene he holds his ground as the key to defending the ships.
